The best initial experiment is **content-conditioned retention inside GRU4Rec**, testing whether selectively retaining recurrent history improves current-intent ranking. No improvement is claimed; the supplied inspiration’s 0.5338 score does not establish this proposal’s performance.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Users reject revived interests and weakly connected recommendations. A history-dependent retention mechanism could address both, although inferred relevance is not observed intent. (2) Electronics has 9.7% wrong-order comparisons and a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin. These identify difficult sampled comparisons, but do not establish HR@10 performance. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply near-zero mean cosine similarity. They provide no basis for an embedding-diversity penalty.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [MTAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) motivates retention mechanisms in recurrent recommendation. It does not establish that time gaps reveal intent changes. (2) [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes always-included positives from sampled negatives. Objective changes therefore require explicit sampling semantics. (3) [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116) supports jointly learned textual representations. Its setting does not establish gains for this sequential benchmark.

The framework separates three directions: **state retention** controls historical influence; **ranking objectives** control competitor separation; **shared item representations** transfer supervision between related items. Diagnose and test these separately before combining changes.

Scores below are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content-conditioned recurrent retention | 4/7/8/6/4 | Directly targets stale-interest revival and weak current connections; may improve confusing comparisons | Overlaps GRU gating; can discard useful long-term preferences; margin benefits are unproven; custom recurrence adds serialization work |
| Sampled listwise loss with uniform negatives | 3/7/5/8/4 | Simple established objective emphasizing competitor separation, particularly relevant to Electronics | Does not directly recover current intent; sampling semantics complicate implementation; transfer from retrieval remains uncertain |
| Joint title/description mean-pooling encoder | 4/7/7/6/6 | Shares supervision across items and may strengthen identifiable media connections | Generic words can reinforce broad relevance; metadata processing adds complexity; sparse supervision may yield poor text features |

Each row’s benefit and limitation applies to its scored dimensions; these are prospective judgments, not measurements.

**Selected experiment.** Replace the fixed recent-history shortcut with a learned retention gate before the existing GRU update. Compute the gate from the previous state and current observed item embedding. This explicitly targets revived older interests and recommendations weakly connected to current activity; improved state discrimination also targets Electronics’ wrong-order comparisons. Compatibility, redundancy, quantity and mood remain unverified.

idea.description: Add a content-conditioned retention gate immediately before each GRU4Rec recurrent update. The gate uses only the current observed item embedding and previous hidden state; all features and scores belong to one jointly trained network per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies revived older interests and weak connections to current activity as distinct recommendation failures. Selective retention could reduce obsolete state influence while retaining useful continuity. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate provides a model-facing target, although neither gate behavior nor margin changes establish improvements in validation HR@10.

idea.pseudocode:
class RetentionGRU(corrected_GRU4Rec):
    initialize():
        retain = Linear(hidden_dim + embedding_dim, 1)
        retain.weight = 0
        retain.bias = 3

    log2feats(sequence):
        h = baseline_initial_state(sequence.batch_size)
        outputs = []
        for t in range(sequence.length):
            valid = sequence[:, t] != 0
            x = baseline_input_transform(item_emb(sequence[:, t]))
            r = sigmoid(retain(concat(h, x)))
            proposed = baseline_gru_cell(x, r * h)
            h = where(valid[:, None], proposed, h)
            outputs.append(where(valid[:, None], h, zeros_like(h)))
        return baseline_feature_projection(stack(outputs, dim=1)) * (sequence != 0)[..., None]

    predict_score(features, items):
        return baseline_scoring_head(features, items)

for category in supplied_four_categories:
    seed_training(42)
    model = RetentionGRU(baseline_configuration)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):

originality.positive: A minimal sequence-only retention intervention offers a distinct test against fixed recent-history pooling while preserving the GRU4Rec interfaces.
originality.negative: GRUs already contain learned gates, and recurrent retention has substantial precedent; this is an incremental architecture hypothesis.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled way to study when historical preferences should persist across four different recommendation domains.
future_potential.negative: Additional forgetting may erase useful long-term signals, and learned gates cannot establish compatibility, intent or redundancy.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one small layer and preserves sequence-only inference, the scoring contract and one-checkpoint deployment.
code_difficulty.negative: Custom recurrent execution may reduce throughput; padding, baseline dropout semantics and predictor serialization require careful parity checks.

related_work.title: MTAM: temporal gating for recurrent recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for temporal gates in recurrent recommendation and short-term preference modeling.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed sequence-only gate.
Time gaps are not observed intent-change labels.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes always-included positive items from sampled negatives when correcting sampled objectives.
limitations: Evidence from retrieval does not establish GRU4Rec HR@10 gains.
Sampling correction does not resolve false negatives or stale user intent.

contributions: Provides precedent for learning textual representations jointly with recommendation supervision.
limitations: Its collaborative-filtering setting differs from this sequential benchmark.
